title: God Is a Spirit Just and Wise
description: God Is a Spirit Just and Wise in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 136, headed “Sincerity and hypocrisy; or, Formality in worship, John 4. 24. Psalm 139. 23 24”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God is a spir-it just and wise, He sees our in-most mind; In vain to heaven we raise our cries And leave our souls be-hind.

lines: God is a spirit just and wise,
In vain to heaven we raise our cries
Nothing but truth before his throne,
Their lifted eyes salute the skies,
Where not the heart is found.
Lord, search my thoughts, and try my ways,
Then shall I stand before thy face,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
